I'm a Research Scientist at the Georgia Tech Research Institute, working on machine learning systems — from topological pipelines for genomic pathogen classification and neural network interpretability (a tool published in PMLR, 2025) to more recent work on multi-agent LLM systems and long-context inference efficiency.

I earned my PhD in Mathematics from the University of Washington (2026), working at the intersection of algebraic geometry, topological data analysis, and machine learning, and received the university's Excellence in Teaching Award. Earlier, I earned a B.A. from Amherst College, where my thesis in discrete Morse theory earned the Robert H. Breusch Prize for the best undergraduate mathematics thesis and was later published in the Annals of Combinatorics (2023).
